html:
Subhas Chandra Bose was an Indian nationalist, born in Cuttack in 1897, who sought help from Germany and Japan to free India and led the Indian National Army in the Second World War.

He passed the exam for the elite Indian Civil Service in 1920 and resigned to join the freedom struggle. He rose fast in the Congress and was elected its president in 1938 and 1939. But he wanted armed struggle and clashed with Gandhi, who opposed him; he resigned in 1939.

In 1941 he escaped house arrest in Calcutta and reached Germany by way of Kabul. He met Hitler and raised a small Indian legion, then in 1943 went by submarine to Japanese held Asia. In Singapore he took command of the Indian National Army and set up a Free India government. Its women's unit was named after Rani Lakshmibai. The army fought with the Japanese at Imphal in 1944 and was beaten.

He died after a plane crash in Taiwan in August 1945. The trials of his officers in 1945 and 1946 stirred great anger in India and helped hasten independence.
sum: Subhas Chandra Bose was an Indian nationalist, born in Cuttack in 1897, who sought help from Germany and Japan to free India and led the Indian National Army in the Second World War.
